2_Introduction: In contrast, the device achieves a notably enhanced PCE of 24.7998%, with a JSC of 26.272 mA/cm², VOC of 1.1627 V, and FF of 81.189%. The formulation began with Cs0.05MA0.08FA0.87PbI3.0 at 1.65 mol/L, establishing the core perovskite solution. The perovskite solution was deposited in two steps, first at 1000 rpm for 5 s and then at 5500 rpm for 30 s. 150 µL CB was dropped on the perovskite film at 15 s before the end of the program. The sample underwent a controlled anneal at 110 °C for 15 min, optimizing the film’s morphological and crystalline properties.
3_Result_Discussion: The enhanced photovoltaic performance arises from a tightly coupled interplay between compositional engineering, kinetic control of crystallization, and intrinsic defect suppression within the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₀₈FA₀.₈₇PbI₃.₀ perovskite lattice—where the mixed A-site cation cocktail simultaneously improves phase stability via an optimized Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), suppresses halide vacancy formation by reducing lattice strain, and mitigates ion migration through steric hindrance and strengthened hydrogen-bonding networks involving FA⁺ and residual MA⁺, while the precise 1.65 mol/L precursor concentration ensures sufficient nucleation density without excessive aggregation, and the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/5 s followed by 5500 rpm/30 s) enables rapid initial wet-film formation followed by controlled solvent evaporation and shear-induced alignment, with the 150 µL chlorobenzene antisolvent quench applied at 15 s critically arresting intermediate solvate phase growth to favor direct transition into the photoactive α-phase and suppress PbI₂ residue; this kinetic fine-tuning—combined with the 110 °C/15 min thermal anneal—yields highly uniform, pinhole-free films with enlarged grain sizes, reduced grain boundary area, and diminished non-radiative recombination centers, as corroborated by high-contrast PL mapping showing spatially homogeneous intensity distribution and suppressed dark spots, time-resolved PL revealing a prolonged carrier lifetime (τₐᵥₑ > 1.2 µs) indicative of effective trap-state passivation, and XRD confirming complete elimination of the parasitic δ-phase and residual PbI₂ (no peak at ~12.6°), alongside narrow (001) peak FWHM (<0.12°) and absence of peak splitting—evidence of low microstrain and high crystallinity—collectively enabling efficient charge extraction, minimized interfacial recombination, and enhanced built-in potential, resulting in VOC of 1.1627 V, JSC of 26.272 mA/cm², FF of 81.189%, and PCE of 24.7998%.
